# BSC (Bharat Steel Group) — Sales Call Knowledge Base (auto-distilled)

## Corpus summary

This corpus is a large concatenation of real call-recordings, but only a modest subset are genuine sales/dealer/customer calls. A significant portion of the transcripts are: (a) internal plant/operations chatter (coil-cutting, machine/operator coordination with "Yuvraj Operator", loading/crane/driver calls), (b) payment/accounts reconciliation calls (debit notes, UTR, invoice copies, Wayman/handling charges disputes), (c) completely unrelated personal/social calls (the many "Vishal" calls are personal/family/cricket/market-gossip conversations in Hindi, not sales calls), and (d) voicemail/wrong-number/silent calls. Genuine sales content — rate enquiries, quantity negotiation, order placement, stock availability, credit/payment terms, objection handling — is scattered across calls with customers/dealers such as V SRIDHAR, Vinayaga Steel Pradeep, Vidveda Krishnasamy/Vignesh, Vasanth Narasimhan Engg, Vijayalakshmi Builder Velmurugan, Zetwork Harish, Vijaya Steels Vijayawada, VJR Developers, VR Earth Movers, Vanniar Narendrakumar, and a few others. This KB is built strictly from those real sales exchanges. Given the heavy dilution with non-sales material, conclusions here are grounded only in what is explicitly said — no invented products, prices, or policies.

## Products & brand ladder

BSC trades in **structural & flat steel products**, not roofing. Products explicitly mentioned across calls:

- **TMT bars / rebar** — grades discussed: **Fe 500, 500D, 550D**. Customers ask "500 kidaikatha sir?" and are told 500D is what's produced; 550 often unavailable ("R&L production இல்ல 3 months-ஆ"). CRS (Chennai Re-rolling Steel?) TMT in 500D also referenced.
- **MS Plates** — thicknesses called out repeatedly: 2mm, 2.5mm, 3mm, 4mm, 5mm, 6mm, 8mm, 10mm, 12mm, 16mm, 20mm, 25mm, 45mm. Standard sizes: 2500mm, 6300mm (most common full-length coil-cut size), 2010/2000mm variants, 4x8, 8x4, 20x4 feet sheets. Checkered plate also sold.
- **Structural sections** — ISMB (I-beam), channels (C-channel, I-channel), MS angles (L-angle, square angle, rectangle angle), flats (25mm, 50x5, 100x5/6), round bars/rods (for bolt threading), square/rectangle pipes (sometimes NOT dealt — "square pipe நம்மகிட்ட இல்ல").
- **CR (Cold Rolled) Coil/Sheet** — CRS mentioned (0.6mm thickness, IS 513 match asked for by a customer sourcing elsewhere); BSC itself does sale CRS 20mm in some calls, sourced via brands.
- **Grades**: E250, E350 (E350 commands **+₹3000** premium over E250 per ton — explicit).
- **Brands/mills referenced as supply sources**: **Sail, Vizag (RINL), JSW, Vaisakh, NMDC** (plates), Tata. Vizag/RINL is repeatedly flagged as "not approved" for some sites ("Vizag is not approved") while being the cheapest/benchmark reference price.
- Company does **not deal**: SHS tube, pipes (CHS pipe — "நாங்க deal பண்றது இல்ல"), square/rectangular pipe.
- Cutting services offered: coil-to-sheet cutting at standard sizes (6300mm full length); customers sometimes request custom cuts (3m) but BSC generally refuses custom flat/angle cutting ("Flats-லாம் நம்ம cut பண்றது கிடையாது") — customer must take full length or pay for a second vehicle.

## Real rates & terms (only rates that actually appear in the calls)

- 8mm sheet, 2500mm: **₹65.5/kg** (quoted), earlier was ₹58–59/kg — rate had risen ~₹1500 in one month.
- Grade upgrade: E250 → E350 = **+₹3000** extra.
- 6mm MS plate, 8x4 size: **₹66–67/kg + GST**, loading/transport extra.
- Structural plates general range quoted multiple times: **₹63–67/kg + tax** depending on thickness (8mm ₹67, 10mm ₹66, 12–32mm ₹63).
- TMT 12mm quoted at **₹69/kg**, 16mm **₹68.5/kg**, GST extra (Saveetha Institute call) — "16 mm கம்மி பண்ண முடியாது 12-க்கு, ₹500 கிடைக்கும் 16-ல".
- Vizag (RINL) benchmark TMT rates (varies by date, shows volatility): ₹62,000/ton, ₹63.5–65/kg range across different calls; Zetwork call: **₹62–63.5/kg** for 12–32mm, with ~₹1500/ton swings day to day.
- 3mm sheet example: rate ₹1500 differential noted; "1250-னா 59500 எடுத்துக்கலாம்" vs ₹1500 differential = full rate.
- Thin plate small-quantity surcharge: "1 number, 2 number கேட்டா ₹5000 கேக்குறாங்க" for 4-feet small plates needing special coil-cut.
- Cutting/wastage charge mentioned: **₹5 per ton** for cutting angles to 3m (customer declined, preferred second vehicle instead).
- Transport/vehicle: 40ft trailer for full-length (12m) TMT; local transport ~₹1800 for 15–16 ton (Trichy–Thuvakudi); ~₹18/kg-equivalent approx for Gudur/Nellore delivery.
- Payment/charge disputes: standard **"payment/handling charge" = ₹200** per vehicle (customer objected to ₹250 being charged once — resolved via debit note).
- Credit terms: **1 month credit** period mentioned (Vidveda Krishnasamy call) — rate for credit differs slightly from advance payment rate.
- Cash & Carry pricing stated as non-negotiable "final rate" in one dealer call (Srividi Engineers/VD Engineer) — vendor refused any ₹500/₹50 paisa discount, held firm on quoted rate.
- Minimum sample policy: 1 meter sample = 1 piece given free for testing; multiple pieces not given for free.

## Objection Playbook

**1. "Rate reduce பண்ணுங்க / Ivvalo kammiya pannunga" (price cut requests)**
- Response pattern: hold firm, cite market increase. "rate எல்லாமே increase ஆயிடுச்சு... கரெக்டா தான் கொடுத்துருக்கோம்." Reps are trained to say the quoted rate is already "wholesale"/"cash and carry" and final — "இந்த rate தான் final."
- When pushed hard, reps sometimes offer a token symbolic discount (₹200–500 out of thousands) rather than real concession — "ஒரு 200 வேணா கம்மி பண்ணி அனுப்புங்க."
- Counter with volume logic: "quantity breakup அனுப்புங்க நான் check பண்ணிட்டு சொல்றேன்" — defers decision without conceding.

**2. "Why did loading/payment/handling charge change suddenly?" (billing disputes)**
- Acknowledge honestly when it's an error: "by mistake-ஆ பண்ணிட்டு இருக்கோம்... debit note raise பண்ணிடுறேன்." Offer to correct via debit/credit note rather than cancelling e-invoice (which is operationally very hard once e-way bill is generated).
- Hold the line on standard charges (e.g., ₹200 payment charge is "standard... every vehicle") while apologizing for one-off inconsistency.

**3. Documentation disputes (missing photo/payment proof at loading)**
- Customer: "camera problem-னு சொல்லி இந்த மாதிரி பண்ணா ஒத்துப்பாங்களா?" Rep apologizes for camera/system failure, offers to regenerate a signed/sealed physical payment copy as compensation — shows willingness to accommodate documentation requests even when system failed.

**4. Stock / grade unavailability**
- Be transparent: "500 கிடைக்காது sir... R&L 3 months-ஆ production இல்ல" — explain root cause (mill production gap) rather than just saying no, which builds credibility and sets expectation for when stock may return.
- For non-standard sizes/cuts: explain operational constraint clearly ("Flats cut பண்றது கிடையாது... balance போறது கஷ்டம்") and offer an alternative (second vehicle, full length purchase, or wait for next coil).

**5. "Vizag rate is cheaper, why can't you match?"**
- Acknowledge Vizag/RINL as benchmark but flag approval status issue: "Vizag is not approved" at certain sites — redirects without disputing the cheaper competitor price directly.

**6. Market volatility objections ("rate ஏறும்ன்னா நீங்க திருப்பி தர்றீங்களா?")**
- Reps do NOT promise future price protection; they redirect to urgency/limited buying strategy instead (see Vasanth Narasimhan calls): "limited stock வாங்குங்க... urgent-க்கு மட்டும்... ரொம்ப வாங்காதீங்க, rate high-ல இருக்கு." This is a notably customer-protective, trust-building objection response — advising against over-buying when prices are at a peak.

**7. Dealer/agent complaining about few leads/conversion ("enquiry கம்மியா வருது")**
- Rep response: be transparent about lead flow reality, commit to sending only relevant ("main") items rather than everything, and set a cadence (e.g., reply within Mon/Wed for Fri/Sat enquiries) to rebuild trust.

## Effective Lines (openings, discovery, closing, follow-up)

**Openings**
- "Hello sir, Good morning, சொல்லுங்க sir" — simple, warm, hands conversation to caller immediately.
- Identify company upfront as caller: "நான் [Company]-ல இருந்து பேசுறேன்" — sets context fast for the BSC rep.

**Discovery (qualifying the enquiry)**
- "என்ன quantity வேணும் sir?" / "எவ்வளவு தேவைப்படுது?" — always quantify before quoting.
- "என்ன size/thickness/grade வேணும்?" — nail down spec before rate discussion (critical given many SKUs).
- "Delivery location எங்க sir?" — transport/rate varies by delivery point, asked early.
- "எந்த company brand வேணும் உங்களுக்கு?" — surfacing brand preference (Sail/Vaisakh/Vizag) drives correct quote.

**Closing**
- "இன்னைக்கு order குடுக்குறேன்" prompts from customers are reinforced by reps with urgency: "payment பண்ணிட்டீங்கன்னா load பண்றதுக்கு ஏற்பாடு பண்ணிடுங
